paragraphs: Direct assessment: If you are willing to coordinate venues, vendors, and on-site work within budgets and deadlines, deliver against contracts and checklists, and manage records, this direction is worth exploring further. The safe trial uses only entirely fictional event requirements, with no real contracts, funds, or venue safety commitments.

Observable signals: Can you turn requirements into executable plans and budgets, check execution against contracts and checklists, and address safety first before escalating unexpected on-site situations? Personality labels cannot determine fit or eligibility.

Conditions supporting fit: Willingness to handle concurrent tasks, intensive communication, and deadline pressure over the long term while maintaining checks and records within budget constraints. Reasons for caution: If unexpected situations and deadline pressure are difficult to tolerate, or on-site safety and coordination responsibilities feel uncomfortable, first compare adjacent directions such as administrative services, public relations, or social service management.

Safe work sample (entirely fictional event requirements): For a fictional group meeting brief, spend 60 minutes writing objectives and a budget, venue and vendor plans, contract and quotation checkpoints, a schedule and execution checklist, on-site safety and emergency steps, and situations requiring confirmation by authorized people. Use no real contracts, funds, or venue commitments.

entries: Plans and budgets: Develop an event plan from requirements and budget, select and coordinate venues and vendors, and check quotations and terms.
Contracts and execution: Manage contracts and settlement, arrange schedules and execution checklists, coordinate on site, handle unexpected situations, and document reviews.

paragraphs: Meeting, convention, and event planners correspond to O*NET 13-1121.00. They coordinate staff, convention personnel, and clients to arrange group meetings, events, and conventions, covering requirements, venues and vendors, budgets and quotations, scheduling and on-site execution, and settlement and review. This page does not equate plans with contracting or funding approval authority.

Work context (O*NET work-context survey, 1–5 scale): Characterized by communication and coordination, concurrent tasks, and deadline pressure, requiring quick responses to unexpected situations on site. Specific context values follow the O*NET work-context survey.

Abilities and work approach: Budget and contract fundamentals, vendor coordination, and on-site organization; the ability to manage concurrent tasks and communicate clearly under deadlines and unexpected situations.

Research inputs: Official O*NET 13-1121.00 description, tasks, work context, interest code ECS, and Job Zone Four, plus BLS 2025 wages and 2024–2034 employment projections for this occupation. These do not establish mainland Chinese qualifications, wages, or employment scope.
Work inputs: Client requirements and budgets, venues and vendors, contracts and quotations, and event safety and insurance requirements.
Inspectable outputs: Plans and quotations, contracts and terms checklists, budgets and settlement, schedules and execution checklists, and on-site records and reviews.
Boundary: This page covers event planning and execution coordination under O*NET 13-1121.00, excluding contracting approval authority, funding decisions, or primary venue safety responsibility.

Adjacent roles are for comparing directions only: This occupation centers on event plans, budgets, and on-site execution; public relations managers handle external communication and relationships; fundraising managers handle fundraising; administrative services managers handle internal operations; social and community service managers handle community programs; and talent agents handle artists' affairs. Qualifications and responsibilities are not interchangeable.

When comparing roles, check each point: Who defines objectives, controls budgets, signs contracts, and bears on-site safety responsibility? Similar titles do not establish equivalent duties or authority.
Difference from public relations managers: They handle external communication and media relations; this occupation handles event plans, budgets, and on-site execution.
Difference from administrative services managers: They handle internal institutional operations and support; this occupation focuses on delivery of specific events.
Difference from fundraising managers: They focus on fundraising goals. This occupation may support communication through events but does not assume fundraising responsibility.

components.definition_block: Meeting, convention, and event planners correspond to O*NET 13-1121.00. They coordinate staff, convention personnel, and clients to arrange group meetings, events, and conventions, covering requirements, venues and vendors, budgets and quotations, scheduling and on-site execution, and settlement and review.

components.work_context_block: O*NET work-context survey for this occupation: 74% report daily time pressure and 76% rate coordinating or leading others as extremely important. These are response percentages from separate questions, not 1–5 scores or a Chinese survey. BLS describes office and event-site work, potentially frequent travel, concurrent tasks and deadlines, many working more than 40 hours weekly, and possible weekend work during events. Check actual arrangements with employers.
